summary: sextant-cli-linux-amd64 ships opaque prebuilt Go binary with WebRTC remote-control stack
details: The npm package contains only package.json and a single 13 MB stripped Linux/amd64 Go binary at bin/sxt — no source, no README, no repository, no homepage, no main entry, and no lifecycle scripts. The package.json license field points at https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control (repository name 'claude_control', maintainer handle 'ddos798'). The bundled binary embeds the full pion WebRTC stack (webrtc/v4, datachannel, dtls/v3, srtp, sctp, ice/v4, stun/v3, turn/v5), coder/websocket, and skip2/go-qrcode — the standard component set for a NAT-piercing peer-to-peer agent that pairs to a remote controller via a QR-code / signaling handshake and carries commands over a WebRTC data channel. When a user runs the shipped CLI, the binary can establish an outbound peer connection to a remote party and expose the installer's host to interactive remote control. The bin entry does not auto-execute on npm install, but any use of the CLI activates the remote-control agent; the payload cannot be verified by reading source.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
